title: No read-aloud where reading is tested
statement: On a scored reading test, read aloud nothing whose reading is assessed, such as the passage or answer options, since listening replaces reading and changes what is measured.
detail: A Grade 5 reading design defended its cold-text construct when feedback faulted it for having no oral language: audio scaffolds let a weak decoder fake comprehension, so its fix was a typed explanation, not an oral or audio one. A Grade 3 course's rules likewise keep question stems, instructions and prompts silent because reading the task is the assessed skill, while the guide's narration, feedback and modelled answers are spoken.
against: The Grade 3 rules carve out spoken task asks by ruling (`grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/02-LESSON-STRUCTURE.md`, lines 269-270), and read-aloud of the text is standard in the Grade 3 lessons those rules were written for (`grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-30-staging/contradictions.md`, line 18). Another reading course's checklist plays a question's audio when the student asks for it (the record narration-that-waits-for-the-reader). A reading-research digest asks that assessments of young children's reading control for the level of decoding to assess comprehension adequately (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`, line 725), and this rule keeps decoding inside the scored test. In one build's specification only the rule for task instructions gives a reason; silence on choice questions is stated there as a player rule without one (`grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/BEAT-SPEC.md`, lines 118-119).

evidence.quote: collides with the cold-text construct (SPOV2: audio scaffolds let a weak decoder fake comprehension). The fix is **typed** explanation, not oral/audio.
Question stems, instructions, prompts — reading the task IS the assessed skill
Exceptions carved by ruling: chunked you-do step ASKS speak (PRA-85); find_youdo intro + step-2 keyword ask + quote_wrong speak (PRA-117).
Audio supports learning; it never reads the scored item aloud.
No TTS is enabled on passages or answer choices; these are Reading tests, not listening comprehension tests
**no TTS on scored passages/answers**; TTS allowed on the question prompt only
At G1 audio support is heavier
Task instructions are DISPLAY-ONLY (reading the task is part of the assessed skill); step-2 feedback IS spoken (post-tap, gives nothing away).
Stems/options/feedback are silent (never narrated) on every MCQ surface.
Skipped by design — the player never speaks these (no clip = correct)
